writing.exampleCaption: Reverse order: the last thing created is the first thing dropped.
writing.explanation: When a value goes out of scope its Drop implementation runs, and values in a scope drop in reverse declaration order. This is deterministic — no collector decides later — which is what lets Rust manage files, locks, and sockets with the same mechanism it uses for memory.
writing.feedback: `a` is dropped early by hand; `b` still drops at the end of the scope.
writing.question: Which of those values drops last?
